title: How Delta Force Works
summary: Josh and Chuck open with news of a September 2008 al-Qaeda bombing of the US embassy in Yemen, then turn to Delta Force, the unofficial US Army special mission unit. They discuss its unofficial status, its origins under Colonel Beckwith after the British SAS model, its link to Special Forces recruiting, its reputed funding through a black fund and related misappropriation investigations, and its reputed missions including Operation Eagle Claw (the 1980 Iran hostage rescue attempt), Operation Just Cause in Panama, and an Indonesia airliner hijacking. They cover reputed recruit marksmanship standards, weapons preferences, the reputed "two tap" method, criticism over the Waco siege, and reputed protective details. Much of the material is acknowledged as hearsay and conjecture.

segments.title: Opening banter and Yemen embassy bombing
segments.summary: Hosts open the show and discuss a recent al-Qaeda car bombing attack on the US embassy in Yemen, including the guard checkpoint confrontation and the broader al-Qaeda presence in Yemen.

segments.title: Why Delta Force is needed and listener warning
segments.summary: Hosts argue that surgical counterterrorism is needed given US entanglements in Iraq and Afghanistan, introduce Delta Force as an unofficial unit, and joke about their admiration for it.

segments.title: Origins of Delta Force and Special Forces background
segments.summary: Hosts describe Delta Force as officially unrecognized, with scant evidence. They discuss Colonel Beckwith, inspired by the British SAS, and how Delta draws its operators from across the branches rather than Special Forces alone. Books and films, including Black Hawk Down and Killing Pablo, and the Chuck Norris and Lee Marvin movies are mentioned.

segments.title: Early missions, Eagle Claw and command structure
segments.summary: Hosts recount Delta's early missions, including guarding the Pan American Games and the 1980 Operation Eagle Claw Iran hostage rescue attempt, which failed after a helicopter crash. They note uncertainty about the unit's chain of command and reputed funding through a black fund.

segments.title: Black fund investigation and Panama operations
segments.summary: Hosts discuss reported misappropriation investigations involving Delta operators and the black fund, then Operation Just Cause in Panama and the capture of Manuel Noriega, noting Delta's reputed role is uncertain.

segments.title: Weapons, marksmanship standards and the two tap method
segments.summary: Hosts describe reputed recruit marksmanship requirements, favored weapons such as the Heckler and Koch MP5 and a Browning .50 caliber sniper rifle, and the reputed two tap method for finishing hostage takers, including a reputed airliner hijacking in Indonesia.

segments.title: Criticism, Waco and closing
segments.summary: Hosts note criticism of Delta over the Waco siege, the military's limits on domestic operations, reported protective details, and their own admiration, then wrap up with a sign-off.
